aspect: A child's prosthesis is replaced roughly annually
description: Growth means refitting or replacement every 12 to 18 months through childhood, each one a cost, a fitting, a period of adjustment and a school absence.
energy_note: A new leg every school year.

description: Components, resins and fitting equipment are imported. Restrictions on banking, shipping and insurance that block medicine block prosthetics the same way, and there is no humanitarian-exemption argument for a pylon.
energy_note: A leg held up by a letter of credit.

aspect: Phantom limb pain, which is neurological and is treated as complaining
description: Real, frequently severe, poorly responsive to ordinary analgesia, and routinely dismissed because the limb in question is not there.
energy_note: Agony in a leg you can see is gone.

aspect: Identity reorganisation is the psychological work, and it is not brief
description: The task is not accepting a lost limb but rebuilding who the person is - worker, parent, partner, body. It takes years and there is usually no psychological support attached to the surgical pathway at all.
energy_note: Surgery in a week, a self in five years.

aspect: SECONDARY - the household reorganises permanently around it
description: One injury converts a spouse into a carer, a child into an assistant, and a two-income household into a none-income household. The measured cost of the injury is the surgery.
